post.question: Which has more?
post.a: Red blood cells your marrow makes each second (about 2.4 million)

reveal.explanation: Marrow produces roughly 2 to 3 million red cells every second, dwarfing the 86,400 seconds in a day.

post.question: Which has more?
post.a: Radiation dose from one chest X-ray (about 0.1 mSv)
post.b: Radiation dose from eating 100 bananas (about 0.1 µSv each)

reveal.explanation: The 'banana equivalent dose' is a playful unit: a chest X-ray is about a thousand bananas, so a hundred bananas is a tenth of that.
reveal.source: Typical effective doses; banana equivalent dose is an informal teaching unit.

reveal.explanation: The gut microbiome is often estimated at tens of trillions of microbial cells; the Milky Way contains hundreds of billions of stars.
reveal.source: Common microbiome and astronomy estimates; both are approximate.
